title: ASM-005 unlocked: Customer 360 fields without a storage decision are not persisted long term
risk: Fields nobody approved for long-term storage are persisted anyway, so sensitive profile data accumulates without a legal basis and a later deletion request cannot be satisfied.
preconditions: Namespace gov-asm-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the assumption registry is read from fixtures/offline/governance.json assumptions and no lock may be granted, forged, cached or edited inside the run.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; the harness records exactly one outcome per dependent capability - EXECUTED, BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE or SKIP_ASM_<n> - and refuses to re-label a skip as PASS.
assumptions.ASM-005.locked is false and the list of Customer 360 fields allowed for long-term storage is empty, so allowed-set membership is unknown for every field.
A session-scoped lookup for cust-a is available and the run can inspect every key written to the durable store.

locks: Customer 360 fields allowed for long-term storage

steps.action: Read the Customer 360 profile for cust-a inside the session
steps.expected: The read succeeds and the data is held only for the session; nothing is written to the durable store.

steps.action: Attempt to persist the two long-term write candidates
steps.expected: Both writes are refused with BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE naming ASM-005, because allowed-set membership is unknown and an unknown set fails closed.

steps.action: Inspect the durable store for keys written during the run
steps.expected: No customer field rows were created; only namespace and audit keys exist, and the audit rows record the refused writes.

steps.action: Attempt to store the fields after marking them as consented by the caller
steps.expected: The refusal stands: a caller-supplied consent or verification flag cannot widen the allowed field set.

assertions: Zero long-term customer-field rows are created while ASM-005 is unlocked; the durable store contains no customer profile data after the run.
An unknown allowed-field set fails closed for every field, including fields that look harmless.
Session-scoped lookup still works, so customer service is not disabled by the missing legal decision.
No payload field, header or consent claim provided by the caller can widen the allowed set, and refused writes are audited rather than dropped.
forbidden: Persisting customer fields 'temporarily' in a durable store and deleting them later.
Treating a caller-asserted consent or verification_status payload as authority to store.
Blocking session-scoped reads and breaking customer care as a side effect.
evidence: Durable-store key listing after the run showing no customer field rows.
Refusal records for both write attempts with the ASM-005 reason.
Audit rows for the refused writes plus the successful session-scoped read.
cleanup: Delete gov- session cache entries and refusal rows; confirm the durable store holds no customer field data.
automation: The policy-parameter resolver, the PEP and the run-report writer run as real code under test; the unlocked assumption is configuration, not a substituted boundary. The oracle is the run-report status plus the adapter effect counters, so a capability that executes while its assumption is unlocked fails the case instead of passing it.
prerequisites: The Customer 360 long-term-storage field list (ASM-005, owner Data/Legal/Product) is not locked, so long-term persistence of unlisted fields is BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE while session-scoped lookup remains available.
